text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging on-call: potential correctness regression detected in prefix prefetch path — increased 5xx for some tenant traffic. See telemetry: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/kv-prefetch/alerts

sara: seeing a spike in 5xx and stale reads for requests that hit prefix-prefetch. pattern: prefetch writes are racing with evictions, causing stale responses for ~0.8% of keys. customers A and C reported incorrect outputs.

mike: are these user-facing errors or internal retries?

sara: user-facing — manifests as corrupted completions or missing memory in chat integrations. error rate up from 0.02% to 1.2% for affected prefixes. p95 latency unchanged.

jia: tagging @mike for oncall handoff, I'm about to propose mitigations.

sara: Proposed live mitigations (short):
- disable prefix prefetch for affected prefix cohort (fastest, correctness-first)
- route affected tenants to kv-bypass pool (reads directly to KV store)
- apply traffic shaping: cap concurrent inflight for problematic tenants to 30rps
- temporarily lower tenant token quotas for noisy tenants to reduce load

kevin: can we disable prefetch with a feature flag?

sara: yes — feature flag: `prefetch.enabled` supports per-namespace override. Command I will run:
```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \ 
  https://admin.redwood.local/featureflags/prefetch.enabled -d '{"namespace":"tenant-42","value":false}'
```

amanda: if we flip that, do we need a cache flush too? I want to avoid mixed state.

sara: good catch. plan: disable prefetch for cohort -> then issue targeted eviction for those prefixes: `kvctl evict-prefix --namespace tenant-42 --prefix pfx123`

ops-bot: NOTE: rolling disable will hit traffic; enabling bypass increases latency ~40ms. Plan accordingly.

mike: I'm taking on-call now — confirming authority to run the flag and evict. @sara please hand off current runbook steps in thread.

sara: handing off. Steps I ran in staging already:
1) disabled prefetch for a single dev tenant and validated no correctness regressions
2) ran evict and verified subsequent reads go to primary KV and are correct
3) measured end-to-end latency impact ~+35ms and error rate dropped to baseline

sara: production plan (my recommended order) — execute with throttle window 5m:
1) `curl` disable prefetch for affected cohort
2) run `kvctl evict-prefix` for hot prefixes in that cohort (parallel limit 10)
3) update routing: add traffic rule to route 10%->bypass to confirm safety, then ramp to 100% if good
4) apply tenant quota cap: `adminctl quota set tenant-42 30rps`
5) monitor key metrics (5xx, stale-read detector, p50/p95)

deploy-bot: deploy pipeline OK for runtime flags. No infra deploy needed.

mike: executing step 1 now. I'll run the curl and report back.

mike: (running) `curl ...prefetch.enabled` -> 200 OK. :white_check_mark:

mike: issuing targeted evictions for the top 5 prefixes now. running `kvctl evict-prefix --namespace tenant-42 --prefix pfx{1..5}`

ops-bot: eviction job queued (job id evict-2039-01). Expecting 60s per prefix.

jia: putting a temporary rate limit rule in place for tenant-42: `iptables`-style ratecap via traffic router config — 30rps. Command: `routectl rate set tenant-42 30rps`

mike: applied ratecap, confirmed in router metrics.

kevin: noticing latency bump but errors trending down. stale-read detector alert resolved for tenant-42.

amanda: any customer-facing comms needed? ops: A and C had support tickets. recommend short note: "We briefly disabled prefetch to protect data correctness; you may see a small latency increase."

mike: drafting message to affected customers; will post after we stabilize for 15m.

sara: monitoring window 15m — if error rate stays <0.05% and stale detector clear, we'll keep fix and schedule a postmortem. If issues remain, plan B is full bypass to primary KV and extend quotas reduction.

incident-bot: page escalation check: owner assigned -> mike, severity -> sev2, start_time -> 2039876543

mike: after 12m metrics look good: 5xx back to baseline, stale reads gone. leaving prefetch off for 24h while we dig root cause.

kevin: starting capture for postmortem: collect prefetch write logs, eviction overlap windows, cache metrics, kernel scheduling traces.

amanda: confirmed customer messages posted to the support tickets. no escalations after update.

sara: follow-ups:
- postmortem owner: sara + kevin
- immediate task: reproduce race in integration harness and add a regression test
- longer term: make prefetch state transitions transactional or add write-ack gating

mike: handing back on-call to sara in 30m. I'll be available for follow-ups.

incident-bot: incident closed to active mitigation phase. next update scheduled by postmortem owners. :white_check_mark:
